title: Serialize chrome.storage read-modify-write to fix lost-update races
description:
The search index in utils/browserSearch.js is a single object in chrome.storage.local, mutated per tab event with readIndex() -> mutate -> writeIndex() and an await in between. chrome.storage has no locking, so concurrent tab events (onCreated/onUpdated/onActivated/onRemoved, plus the extra listeners in background.js) interleave and clobber each other's writes — entries silently dropped, especially during session restore / bulk tab open. Symptom: search misses tabs that are actually open.

Same read-mutate-write-storage pattern recurs and should be fixed consistently:
- utils/workspaceManager.js (workspaces/assignments)
- components/WorkspaceLane.js reorderInStorage (tabOrder) and the collapse handler (collapsedLanes)

Fix direction: route all index/state mutations through a single serialized write queue (chain mutations through one promise so they can't interleave), or hold the index as an in-memory source of truth with debounced persistence. Related: rebuildIndex() was made merge-not-overwrite as an interim mitigation (see reviewer fix) — fold that into the proper serialization so startup and live writes share one path. Repro: open ~20 tabs rapidly, then search; confirm all appear.
label: Bug

activity.content:
Implemented serialized `chrome.storage.local` read-modify-write operations across the affected state paths.

- Added a reusable per-key mutation queue that remains usable after failed mutations.
- Routed tab search event updates, metadata extraction, removal/activation updates, and startup rebuilding through the queue. Startup rebuilding now merges queried tabs into the latest queued index.
- Routed workspace and assignment mutations through the same helper, including schema normalization/initialization.
- Serialized `tabOrder` reorders and `collapsedLanes` toggles.
- Added regression coverage simulating 20 concurrent index mutations and queue recovery after failure.

Validation:
- `node --test tests/storageMutationQueue.test.mjs` - 2 tests passed.
- `node --check` across all JavaScript under `utils/` and `components/` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed (line-ending notices only).
